transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 09:00 PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Alex, Priya, Tomás, Lara, Ethan, Nora (and a few on mute)

Summary (auto): validate fallback capacity and launch gating ahead of private pilot.

[00:00] Maya: All right folks, thanks for joining early, we've got a packed agenda. The goal is simple — make sure our fallback lane behaves predictably under stress so the pilot doesn't cascade into customer impact. I'm gonna hand it to Alex for a quick state of infra readiness.

[00:20] Alex: Yeah hi, quick update — infra is green for the baseline config. We've provisioned the dedicated GPU pools for the pilot region, but the fallback capacity pool is only partially warmed; we can cover baseline QPS but not sustained double-spike for more than ~20 minutes right now. There may be pre-warm slowdowns when we spin up extra nodes, and we saw a 10-15% p99 blip during last week's burst test.

[00:48] Priya: When you say "partially warmed" — is that because of constraints with image boot or because of NVMe initialization? I remember Lara had a note that some kernels take longer to JIT on new machines.

[01:05] Lara: It's a mix. The node boot is fine, but the runtime kernel warm-up (quantization path) with the model shard causes a spike. Also K V cache repopulation is slow on cold starts, so the first 1k requests see higher tail latencies. We're working on a pre-warm hook but it's not fully baked.

[01:36] Tomás: Just to add — the runtime can be configured to keep a warmed K/V cache snapshot that we can inject at node start. It's an option but it increases memory footprint. If we enable it for fallback nodes, the cold-start tail improves but cost goes up. Tradeoff.

[02:02] Ethan: Tradeoffs noted. For the pilot customer's SLA we promised a percent of requests served with < 300ms median. We need to define the fallback SLA separately: what are we willing to degrade to and for how long.

[02:25] Maya: Right. Proposal: fallback lane should aim for p50 < 400ms and p95 < 1.2s for up to 20 minutes of sustained burst. Beyond that, degrade gracefully by shedding batch-size and reduce tokens-per-second. Thoughts?

[02:50] Alex: I think that's reasonable as long as the canary detects capacity pressure and triggers an automated scale-up or route to cold fallback. We need clear metrics that trigger those transitions.

[03:12] Nora: For QA I'll need deterministic scenarios. I'd like two simulations: (A) microburst 30s at 3x QPS, (B) sustained 25-minute 1.8x QPS to test degradation. Each should log KV hit-rate, p99/p95, and memory pressure.

[03:40] Priya: Good call. We'll also need to ensure privacy/data residency checks are green during those simulations — don't leak keys or telemetry. Legal asked that we confirm no unredacted logs are exported to external buckets during tests.

[04:02] Lara: noted, we can set test sandbox with local KMS and strict retention.

[04:18] Maya: Tomás, can you sketch the OOM sim plan? I know you had a draft.

[04:30] Tomás: Yeah. The plan is to simulate KV cache pressure by artificially limiting memory available to the process and then pushing synthetic long-context generation to force KV growth. We'll run with two quantization profiles: int8 and int4 to see behavior differences. We'll instrument the run to capture kernel-level metrics and Runtime traces. There may be noise when the kernel swaps, so expect some lost spans.

[05:05] Alex: When we do that, we should exercise both the primary lane and the fallback lane simultaneously to test routing logic — we don't want rules that look good in isolation but cause thrash under blended traffic.

[05:28] Tomás: Agree. Also, note that some of our fallback heuristics are heuristic; they compute an estimated cost per token and switch lanes when cost > threshold, but we haven't tuned it for long context sessions.

[05:49] Maya: OK. Action — Tomás to run the sim in staging and post results. We'll need a short video and a spreadsheet of metrics to share.

[06:00] Ethan: Dashboard changes — we need a new card on the console: 'fallback-lane usage' with flags for threshold triggers, current pool capacity, and ramp times. Also a 'cold-start tail' chart. I'll take that, but need a concrete API from runtime for metrics.

[06:23] Tomás: I can add a lightweight /metrics endpoint that exposes cache fill-rate, allocated memory, and a fallback-trigger flag. It won't be perf-heavy.

[06:36] Priya: For launch gating, I want three primary gates: (1) no critical regressions on canary regression set, (2) fallback activation must maintain customer-impact SLOs (explicit numbers), (3) runbook and playbook approved by SRE and ops. If any gate fails we stop.

[07:05] Maya: Let's codify gate (2) as p95 latency under failover < 1.2s and error-rate increase < 0.5% absolute. Does that sound right?

[07:21] Alex: 0.5% seems tight but doable. We should also define that the fallback lane can be disabled remotely as a last-resort throttle.

[07:40] Lara: There was a mention in legal that we need auditable logs of any fallback routing decision for compliance — SSO and audit trail. We should ensure distributed tracing includes a fallback decision tag.

[08:01] Nora: QA will add an assert that fallback-routing headers are present and that traces include the reason code.

[08:14] Maya: Great. Comms: if we hit a fallback event in pilot, we will notify the customer success lead and the account owner within 5 minutes and we'll send a post-mortem within 48 hours. Priya, can you own the comms template?

[08:35] Priya: Yep, I'll draft a transparent notification template and post-mortem template.

[08:44] [small crosstalk] Ethan: Quick ops question — do we want to pre-warm fallback nodes with a warmed cache snapshot? Costly but reduces tail.

[09:02] Tomás: As I said earlier, pre-warm snapshot is an option. For the pilot maybe we pre-warm 1 node per shard and see impact. If cost is an issue we can run a fast warm-up hook that replays some common prefixes.

[09:25] Maya: Can we get cost delta numbers? If pre-warm adds 22% memory overhead, what's the monthly incremental? Lara, can you estimate?

[09:36] Lara: Rough estimate: pre-warm snapshot will add about 0.18 vGPU-hours per node per day if we keep warm 24/7; scaled to pilot region it's about $3k/mo. If we only pre-warm during business hours it's ~1k/mo.

[09:55] Priya: That seems manageable for pilot. Let's document both options in the runbook with cost callouts.

[10:06] Maya: Let's discuss alerts and pages. Alex, what's the current on-call flow?

[10:12] Alex: Pager flow: critical fallback trigger hits -> immediate P0 page to SRE primary; secondary gets notified if ack > 5m; ops lead gets email as well. We need a playbook that lists quick mitigation steps: disable fallback lane, scale up nodes, flip to read-only, rollback model. We'll attach runbook steps to pager.

[10:38] Nora: QA will write a checklist that on-call can tick off during an event. We'll also include quick-commands for infra.

[10:47] Maya: Okay, timeline. We need these things before the pre-launch smoke date: metrics card and instrumented metrics by 03-24; runbook and QA sims by 03-23; legal signoff by 03-26; exec go/no-go by 03-27. Does that align?

[11:05] Ethan: Yes that's workable but it's tight. We might need to deprioritize a non-blocking feature like warmed snapshot until after pilot.

[11:18] Tomás: For the OOM sim I'll run the int4/int8 runs and attach kernel-level traces. Note: the runtime's current trace retention is 2 hours; we should bump to 24 hours for post-mortem. That requires a config change.

[11:36] Lara: Approved — we can bump retention for staging runs only. For prod we'll keep lower retention.

[11:44] Maya: Any blockers from security?

[11:48] Priya: Security asked to confirm KMS key scopes for staging runs and to ensure no plaintext logs are shipped to external buckets. I'm expecting a sign-off by 03-20.

[12:00] Maya: All right. Let's recap real quick.

[12:05] Maya: Recap: Tomás runs OOM sim and shares traces (due 03-22). Lara & Nora produce the runbook and QA sims (due 03-21 / 03-23). Ethan adds metrics card (03-24). Maya will get legal/exec signoff (03-26 / 03-27). Priya drafts comms. If all gates pass, we proceed to pilot launch.

[12:30] Alex: One more thing — we should test competitor failure modes. Vertex/Bedrock sometimes have a long tail on cold start; let's validate our fallback behaves better in our simulated long-context test. Not a blocker but a benchmark.

[12:50] Priya: I'll schedule a short benchmarking session after the sim runs.

[13:05] Maya: OK, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the #pilot-fallback channel and I'll post the checklist. Meeting adjourned.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few mis-hears (K V cache sometimes transcribed as K V cash; JIT/jit as GIT) — QA verified the key technical terms.
